claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: Assume S meets all listed cycles. If G-S had a cycle, a shortest one would be chordless, hence induced. Bipartiteness makes its length even. Length at least 10 is impossible because eight consecutive vertices induce P8; therefore it would be an unhit C4, C6, or C8. The converse is immediate. Thus G-S is a forest. Each component is a tree whose diameter path is induced, so P8-freeness bounds its diameter by 6 and its radius by 3. If S is inclusion-minimal, restoring any x creates a cycle that must contain x; deleting x from that cycle leaves a path in one component of G-S between two distinct neighbors of x.
claims.search_method: Direct shortest-cycle and tree arguments, supplemented by exhaustive checking of every vertex subset in all 512 bipartite graphs with a fixed 3-by-3 bipartition.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: There are O(n^8) candidate subsets for induced C4, C6, and C8 enumeration. By claim 0, FVS is exactly the resulting rank-eight hitting-set problem. At an uncovered edge, every size-k solution contains one of its at most eight vertices, giving an exhaustive depth-k search tree with O(8^k) nodes and O(8^k n^8) time. For approximation, scan the cycle list to obtain a maximal vertex-disjoint packing and return its union U. Every listed cycle intersects U by maximality, so U is an FVS. If the packing has p cycles, OPT is at least p while |U| is at most 8p, proving the factor 8.
claims.search_method: Independent reduction and search-tree analysis; exact comparison of obstruction hitting, branching decisions, greedy packing output, and brute-force FVS optimum on all 512 fixed-3-by-3 bipartite graphs.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: The exact enumeration independently reproduced survivor counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for ordered-path orders 1 through 15. At each extension it considers every possible edge from the new path vertex to earlier opposite-parity vertices, while forcing the next path edge and rejecting exactly graphs containing a C4 or induced P8. Hence any bipartite C4-free P8-free graph containing a 15-vertex simple path would yield a survivor at order 15, contradicting the zero count. In an undirected DFS every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints. Bags consisting of each vertex and its ancestors cover every edge and have connected occurrence sets; disconnected DFS trees can be joined at their roots without changing bags. A root-to-leaf path has at most 14 vertices, so the width is at most 13. A fixed-width connectivity-partition dynamic program then solves FVS in polynomial time.
claims.witness: Ordered-path survivor certificate: 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0, with no survivor on 15 vertices.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive integer-bitmask generation of every bipartite supergraph of a fixed ordered path, followed by an independent verification of the DFS ancestor-bag decomposition.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: Branching on all four vertices of an uncovered C4 is exhaustive because every C4-transversal must choose one of them. Iterative deepening through depth r therefore finds a minimum transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. The hereditary graph G-X is C4-free, P8-free, and bipartite, so claim 2 supplies a width-13 decomposition. Adding X to every bag gives width at most r+13 and covers edges incident with or internal to X. For a width-t decomposition, FVS states consist of the deleted bag subset and a partition encoding connectivity among retained vertices; there are at most 2^t times the Bell number of t vertices, hence 2^{O(t log t)} states. Standard introduce-edge and join consistency tests reject exactly cycle-forming combinations, yielding the stated FPT bound.
claims.search_method: Parameterized branching analysis, exact state-count bound, and finite exhaustive validation of minimum C4-transversal branching plus residual and augmented tree decompositions on all 512 fixed-3-by-3 bipartite graphs.

claims.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
claims.evidence: In the half-graph H_n, all neighborhoods are distinct and nested, so there are no false twins and no induced 2K2; consequently it is P5-free. Retaining all B vertices and a_{n-1},a_n is C4-free. Conversely, if a C4-free retained set contains two least-indexed A vertices a_i,a_j with i<j, at most one of their common neighbors b_j,...,b_n remains. Thus at most j B vertices and at most n-j+2 A vertices remain, for at most n+2 vertices total; the C4-transversal number is exactly n-2. For the theta graph with m length-three u-v paths, every cycle uses two branches and has length six, deletion of any vertex leaves the graph connected, and an induced path has at most six vertices; these are arbitrarily large 2-connected C4-free P8-free graphs. Finally, K_{3,3} is P4-free and has FVS optimum 2, while weight 1/4 on each vertex satisfies every induced-C4 constraint with objective 3/2, strictly below the integral optimum.
claims.witness: H_n with edges a_i b_j iff i≤j; the theta graph with paths u-a_i-b_i-v; and K_{3,3} with uniform LP weight 1/4.
claims.search_method: Symbolic family proofs plus exact checks for H_n at n=2 through 7, theta graphs with 2 through 8 branches, and K_{3,3} using integer bitmasks and Fraction arithmetic.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a polynomial-time exact Feedback Vertex Set algorithm on all P8-free bipartite graphs. The draft does not prove that target and explicitly disclaims doing so. Claim 1 gives an exponential-in-k exact algorithm and an approximation; claim 2 is polynomial only under C4-freeness; claim 3 is exponential in a C4-transversal parameter that claim 4 shows is unbounded on the target class. These are correct and material partial advances, while the final writeup does not overclaim their coverage. Accordingly, target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is accurate.
